title: I Took the DMV Kiosk Timestamp to the Clerk Who Called Me Late

parts.text: I checked in at the kiosk at 2:14 p.m. for a 2:15 appointment. At the window the clerk said I was next-day late. The appointment policy on the ticket said: KIOSK TIME GOVERNS. GRACE TEN MINUTES. I was forty-five, taking unpaid leave, holding a 2:14 printout. Clerk Dara said, "Kiosks lie." I pointed at the policy. She closed the window flag. "Windows don't lie." I photographed the printout, the policy, and the closed flag. Then I took the timestamp to the floor supervisor. At 2:18 the supervisor asked why Dara's window was on a false-late ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The supervisor can see a 2:14 kiosk time against a next-day late call.

social.video_title: The clerk called a 2:14 kiosk next-day late — Part 1/2
social.description: Unpaid leave, a grace policy, and a closed flag. I walked the timestamp. Would you have rebooked a month out?

parts.text: Dara called it a queue glitch until the supervisor pulled the kiosk log. I printed the ticket, the policy, and the photo. I got the window. Dara told the line the policy was always about optics. Optics is a word clerks use when a kiosk exists. Appointment policy now has a second line: WINDOWS DO NOT OVERRIDE KIOSKS. I renewed. Dara flags on time. The number display finally matches the paper.

social.video_title: Windows do not override kiosks — Part 2/2
social.description: False-late ticket, a real window, and a second line on the policy. Was a glitch ever next-day?
